# Next Org Chart

Next Collection org chart that builds a reporting hierarchy from report rows (ID and PARENT_ID, in any order) in five layouts, each made for one job. Top-down (depth) is the classic chart for leadership pages: people sit on name plates, a collapsed team becomes a stack of plates whose thickness shows its size, and teams of individual contributors stack vertically to save width. Left to right (smart) suits deep chains such as a directorate structure and turns into an indented outline in narrow regions. Department swimlanes (bold) give each department a lane with its headcount and open seats, for restructuring and workforce planning. Radial (motion) puts a small project team around its lead, and branches grow out of their manager when opened. Staff directory (smart) is a searchable list grouped under managers that filters as you type and shows each person's chain of command. All layouts share collapsible branches, search that reveals and scrolls to a person, keyboard tree navigation, zoom and drag to pan for large charts, and a hatched empty plate for vacant positions. Without JavaScript the rows show as an outline list indented by Level.

| | |
|---|---|
| Plug-in type | templateComponent |
| Static ID | `AMC_NEXT_ORG_CHART` |
| APEXlang reference | `type: plugin/nextOrgChart` |
| Modes | report (multiple rows) |
| Minimum APEX | 23.1 (APEXlang import: 26.1+) |
| Version | 1.0.0 |

One query row per position. Map ID (required) and Parent ID: the ID of the manager's row, empty for the top of the chart. Rows may arrive in any order; a CONNECT BY query with ORDER SIBLINGS BY and LEVEL gives the best result without JavaScript. Name is the person, Job Title their role, Department groups the swimlanes. Set Vacant to Y for an open position; its Name may stay empty. Headcount is the size of the whole team under a person; when empty the chart counts the people it has. The runtime file builds the tree, search, keyboard navigation and zoom, and rebuilds after a region refresh.

## Settings

| APEXlang setting | Builder label | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | Style | selectList (`topDown`, `leftToRight`, `swimlanes`, `radial`, `directory`) | yes | `topDown` | Layout of the chart; the direction is given in brackets as motion, depth, bold or smart. topDown [depth]: the classic chart for a leadership or intranet page; name plates joined by connectors, a collapsed team shows as a stack of plates, and teams without managers below them stack vertically. leftToRight [smart]: each level is a column, for deep hierarchies such as a ministry's directorates; in regions narrower than about 560px it becomes an indented outline. swimlanes [bold]: one lane per Department with its people, headcount and vacant positions, for restructuring and workforce planning; a lane's top person shows who they report to in another department. radial [motion]: the lead in the centre and the team on rings around them, for project teams of up to about 25 people; opened branches grow out of their manager. directory [smart]: a staff directory grouped under managers; search filters the list and each result shows its chain of command. |
| `id` | ID | sessionStateValue | yes |  | Unique key of the row, for example the position or employee ID. Parent ID of the people who report to this row refers to it. |
| `parentId` | Parent ID | sessionStateValue |  |  | ID of the manager's row. Leave empty for the top of the chart. A row whose manager is not in the query, or that would create a loop, is shown as another top-level person, so a filtered query still renders. |
| `name` | Name | sessionStateValue |  |  | Person's name, for example Noura Al-Qahtani. May be empty for a vacant position, which then reads Vacant position. |
| `title` | Job Title | sessionStateValue |  |  | Job title in sentence case, for example Head of treasury or Warehouse manager, Jebel Ali. Search also matches it. |
| `department` | Department | sessionStateValue |  |  | Department or unit, for example Finance or Customs and trade compliance. It makes the lanes of the swimlanes style, where rows without a department go to an Other lane, and search matches it. |
| `imageUrl` | Image URL | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional photo URL, for example from apex_util.get_blob_file_src or an Object Storage link. Shown as a round portrait; when empty the Initials are shown. |
| `initials` | Initials | sessionStateValue |  |  | One or two letters shown when there is no photo, for example NQ. Compute them in SQL, for example upper(substr(first_name, 1, 1) \|\| substr(last_name, 1, 1)). |
| `linkUrl` | Link URL | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional target of the person's name, usually built in SQL with apex_page.get_url, for example to the employee record. Enter on a focused person opens it. The URL must come from the developer, not from user input. |
| `vacant` | Vacant | sessionStateValue |  |  | Y for an open position, N or empty for a filled one; yes and no are also accepted. Vacant positions show as a hatched, dashed plate labelled Vacant position, and are counted separately in team and lane totals. |
| `headcount` | Headcount | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional whole number: people in this person's whole team, for example 214 for a head of operations whose team is not all in the query. When empty the chart counts the filled positions below the person that are in the query. |
| `level` | Level | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional depth, 1 for the top, usually LEVEL from a CONNECT BY query ordered with ORDER SIBLINGS BY. Only used to indent the outline list shown without JavaScript, up to 8 levels; the runtime file works out the tree from Parent ID. |
| `expandLevels` | Open Levels | integer |  | `2` | Number of levels open when the chart loads, 1 to 12. With 2 the top person and their direct reports are visible and deeper teams start collapsed. Search opens any branch it needs. The staff directory always opens every level. |
| `showSearch` | Show Search | yesNo |  | `Y` | Y shows a Find a person field above the chart that matches names, job titles and departments, opens the branches it needs and scrolls to the person. N hides it, for small charts. |

## Install

- **APEX 26.1+ with APEXlang:** copy `dist/apexlang/shared-components/plugins/next-org-chart/` into your app's `shared-components/plugins/`, then run the apexlang skill's format, compiler-truth and runtime validate gates.
- **APEX 23.1 to 25.x (or any version, via App Builder):** import `dist/legacy/amc_next_org_chart.sql` from Shared Components > Plug-ins > Import.
